items.text: The trio had no set approach beyond looking for unique moments in the music and capturing them.
items.why: Production: 'The group had no set approach to working beyond looking for and capturing unique moments'; 'trio' from 'The trio shared a house'.
Production: 'recorded in Hamilton, Ontario in 1984'; Infobox: 'Studios: Grant Avenue Studio, Hamilton, Ontario'.

items.text: The Pearl is the pair's second album together, after Ambient 2: The Plateaux of Mirror (1980).
items.why: Lead: 'second collaborative studio album by Harold Budd and Brian Eno'; 'previous collaboration, Ambient 2: The Plateaux of Mirror (1980)'.

items.text: Like Ambient 2, it is built mostly from subtly treated piano textures, with noticeable electronic treatments and recordings of nature added.
items.why: Lead: 'consisting mostly of subtly treated piano textures, but with more pronounced electronic treatments and nature recordings'. The pack says the treatments and nature recordings are MORE pronounced than on Ambient 2; 'added' implies they are new to The Pearl.

items.text: Budd says the two albums are alike in sound and timbre, and that the likeness was there from the start of production.
items.why: Comparison: 'similar in terms of sounds and timbres, and those similarities were conceived even during the onset of production'.

items.text: Ambient 2 came together effortlessly, and the duo believed they could make similar music again without much trouble.
items.why: Comparison: 'The former album was produced effortlessly, and the duo thought they could produce similar music again with ease'.

items.text: Budd said The Pearl was harder to make. He put this down to the duo's naivety on Ambient 2, and to a musical language that had matured since.
items.why: Comparison: 'production on The Pearl was more challenging. Budd attributed this to naivety ... their musical language had matured since then'.

items.text: For the length of the sessions, the three stayed in one house and worked seven days a week.
items.why: Production: 'The trio shared a house during the recording sessions and worked on the record seven days per week'.

items.text: Recording took two weeks, and finishing the record took 8 to 12 months, as they worked out which pieces suited each other.
items.why: Production: 'recorded over two weeks, and then it took 8-12 months to finish production and decide which tracks worked best together'.

items.text: Eno made most of the aesthetic calls and spent hours working alone, recording pieces at varied speeds.
items.why: Production: 'Eno made most of the decisions on aesthetics, spending hours working solo and recording pieces at different speeds'.

items.text: Among the pianos were an acoustic one and electric models by Yamaha and Rhodes.
items.why: Production: 'an acoustic piano, as well as Yamaha and Rhodes electric pianos'.

items.text: The treatments came from gear that included a Yamaha DX7, a Sequential Circuits Pro One, an AMS digital delay and an Eventide Harmonizer.
items.why: Production: 'For treatments, the group used a Yamaha DX7, ... a Sequential Circuits Pro One, AMS digital delay, Eventide Harmonizer'.

items.where: listen_for: Lost in the Humming Air
items.text: Budd improvises over humming tones that Eno plays on a Yamaha CS-80, in a single take.
items.why: Production: 'Budd improvised to humming noises by Brian Eno played on a Yamaha CS-80 and recorded in one take'. Title matches the track list.

items.text: Budd laid it down first at a small studio, and Eno then reworked it, which Budd calls an extreme version of how the pair worked.
items.why: Production: 'Budd recorded it at a small studio beforehand and sent to Eno to develop further; this, according to Budd, was the "extreme version" of how they worked'. Title matches the track list.

missed: How it sounds to listeners in the pack: Sound on Sound's oceanic imagery (galleons at the bottom of the sea, fish swimming silently) and Electronics & Music Maker's 'mix of Eno's melancholia and Budd's optimism'; also Budd's view that it is more 'cohesive' and 'focused' than Ambient 2.
